_about: Edit to change what each theme means: an entry is matched to the themes whose examples it most resembles. After editing, regenerate the vectors: scripts/dev-run.sh --maintenance.task=generate-themes (then commit the file it writes). 'everyday' entries have no theme; they set the threshold below which an entry gets no theme. Keep examples varied: short and long, direct and implied, in a journal's first-person voice.

themes.name: anxiety
themes.meaning: Worry, dread or nerves about what might happen.
examples: Couldn't sleep, my mind kept replaying everything that could go wrong tomorrow.
Heart racing before the presentation, hands shaking. I kept thinking I'd forget everything.
Felt on edge all day for no reason. Checked my phone constantly waiting for bad news.
Worried about money again. Kept running the numbers over and over in my head.
I had a knot in my stomach the whole commute thinking about the email from my manager.
What if I fail the exam, what if I lose the place, what if everyone sees. The what-ifs won't stop.
My partner was an hour late home and didn't answer his phone. I'd imagined every possible accident before he walked in.
Results day is Thursday. Keep checking the website even though I know they're not out yet.
Sunday evenings are the worst. Feel dread creeping in about the week before it's even started.
Had to make a phone call to the council and rehearsed it for twenty minutes first. Voice still shook.

themes.name: burnout
themes.meaning: Running on empty: exhausted, numb, and losing interest in things that used to matter.
examples: I'm exhausted all the time. Even things I used to enjoy feel like chores.
Worked late every night this month. I don't feel stressed anymore, just empty.
Took a day off but couldn't rest. My brain just felt numb and flat.
I keep going through the motions at work. Nothing feels like it matters.
Cried in the car before work. I've got nothing left in the tank.
Weekend came and I slept most of it and still feel drained.
Looked at my calendar for next week and just closed the laptop. There's no gap anywhere, and I can't remember the last evening I had to myself.
Made a mistake at work I'd never normally make. I'm so tired I'm not thinking straight anymore.
Everyone says take a break, but even breaks feel like another thing to organise.
Snapped at a colleague, forgot to eat lunch, fell asleep on the sofa at 8. That's most days now.

themes.name: confidence
themes.meaning: Trusting yourself and acting on it.
examples: Led the meeting today and it went really well. I trusted my judgement and it paid off.
I asked for the raise and got it. I'm proud I backed myself.
Gave my first talk and actually enjoyed it. I felt like I knew my stuff.
Stood my ground in a disagreement calmly. I'm more sure of myself than I used to be.
Signed up for the half marathon. A year ago I wouldn't have believed I could.
Shared my writing publicly for the first time and felt good about it, whatever people think.
Sent my portfolio to the agency I've always wanted to work with. Old me would have waited until it was 'ready'.
Spoke to the new neighbours and introduced myself. Small, but it used to terrify me.
Told my manager I disagreed with the plan and explained why. She actually changed it.
Looked in the mirror before the date and thought, you know what, I look good.

themes.name: discipline
themes.meaning: Doing what you planned even when you don't feel like it.
examples: Didn't feel like training but went anyway. Five weeks without missing a session now.
Kept to my rule of no phone before 9am. The mornings feel so much calmer.
Did my 30 minutes of revision even though I was tired. Showing up is what counts.
Stuck to my budget this week for the first time. Took effort to say no to takeaways.
Woke up at 6 again. The routine is starting to feel automatic rather than forced.
I set myself a schedule for the week and actually followed it, even the boring bits.
No caffeine after 2pm for a month now. Annoying some afternoons but I'm sleeping better.
Same routine: write 500 words before breakfast, every day, even the ones where the words are rubbish.
Wanted to skip physio exercises tonight but did them anyway in front of the telly.
Day 60 of learning Spanish on the train. Some sessions are five minutes but I haven't missed one.

themes.name: emotional regulation
themes.meaning: Noticing strong feelings and choosing how to respond to them.
examples: Felt the anger rising when he interrupted me, so I took a breath before replying. It helped.
I was close to snapping at my sister but went for a walk first and came back calmer.
Noticed I was spiralling, named the feeling, and let it pass instead of reacting.
Lost my temper at the kids today and felt awful. Trying to work out what set me off.
Used the breathing exercise when I got overwhelmed in the shop. It took the edge off.
My mood swung from fine to furious in seconds. I want to understand what triggers it.
Got a nasty email and started typing a furious reply. Saved it as a draft, went for a run, and sent something calm an hour later.
Felt panic rising in the queue so I named five things I could see. It passed.
I went quiet and sulked all evening instead of saying I was hurt. Want to handle that better next time.
Noticed I get irritable when I'm hungry. Ate something before replying to mum this time and it went much better.

themes.name: gratitude
themes.meaning: Noticing and appreciating the good things and people in your life.
examples: Grateful for my mum's phone call this morning. Small thing but it made my whole day lighter.
Three things I'm thankful for: a hot shower, my friend's terrible jokes, and the quiet walk home.
Noticed how lucky I am to have a warm flat and food in the fridge. Easy to forget.
My colleague covered for me when I was ill and I realised how much I appreciate the people around me.
Sat in the park and just felt thankful to be healthy and here.
Really appreciated my partner cooking dinner tonight without me asking.
Long, rough week, but my brother turned up with pizza and we watched rubbish films until midnight. Exactly what I needed.
The nurse who looked after dad was so gentle with him. I keep thinking about how much that meant.
Woke up early and watched the sunrise from the kitchen window. Felt like a gift.
My old teacher replied to my message and said she remembered me. Made me so happy.

themes.name: motivation
themes.meaning: The drive to work towards something, or the struggle to find it.
examples: Feeling really fired up about my new project. I can't wait to get started tomorrow.
Lost all drive this week. I know what I want but can't make myself care.
Reminded myself why I started and it gave me a burst of energy to keep going.
Some days I'm buzzing with ideas, other days I can't get off the sofa.
Watching my progress chart go up is keeping me going.
I've lost sight of why I'm doing this course. Need to find my reason again.
Ran my first 10k and immediately looked up half marathons. I want to see what else I can do.
Wrote down my goals for the year and they feel like someone else's. Not sure what I'm working towards anymore.
Finally found a reason to save: the trip to Japan. Suddenly cutting back feels easy.
I keep starting things with loads of energy and dropping them after two weeks.

themes.name: perfectionism
themes.meaning: Holding yourself to a standard where anything less than perfect feels like failure.
examples: Spent three hours on one slide because the alignment didn't look right.
Got 92 percent and all I can think about is the 8 percent I lost.
I won't post anything until it's flawless, so I've posted nothing in months.
Rewrote the opening paragraph ten times and still hate it.
Missed the deadline because I kept polishing something that was already good enough.
If it isn't perfect I feel like I've failed, even when everyone else says it's great.
Spent the whole weekend re-recording one song because of a tiny wobble in the second verse that nobody else can hear.
Haven't started the blog because I can't decide on the perfect name and design.
The cake tasted great but it leaned slightly so I didn't take it to the party.
My manager said the report was excellent. I only see the typo I found after sending it.

themes.name: procrastination
themes.meaning: Putting off something that matters, often by doing easier things instead.
examples: Spent the whole afternoon tidying my desk and reorganising files instead of starting the essay.
I said I'd begin at 10, then 11, then after lunch. It's 9pm and I haven't opened the document.
Watched three episodes 'as a break' before even starting. The deadline is tomorrow and I feel sick about it.
Every time I sit down to do my tax return I suddenly need to do something else first.
I keep putting off calling the dentist. It's a two-minute call and it's been on my list for a month.
Left the assignment until the night before again and pulled an all-nighter. Swore I wouldn't do that this time.
Cleaned the oven for the first time in a year. The CV is still exactly where I left it on Monday.

Kept telling myself I'd start the revision once I'd had a coffee, then once I'd checked my emails, then once the washing was out. Now it's dark and I've done none of it, and I'm annoyed at myself all over again.
My plan for the morning was the budget spreadsheet. I made a to-do list for the spreadsheet instead.
Renewing my passport has been on the list since spring. The trip is in three weeks.

themes.name: self-doubt
themes.meaning: Doubting your own ability or worth, even when things go well.
examples: Got the job offer but I keep thinking they made a mistake and will realise I'm not good enough.
I didn't speak up in the meeting because I was sure my idea was stupid. Someone else said the same thing and got praised.
Everyone on my course seems to understand this except me. Maybe I'm just not cut out for it.
I rewrote the text to my friend four times because I was worried it sounded wrong.
Even when people compliment my work I assume they're just being nice.
Felt like a fraud presenting today, like any minute someone would expose that I don't know what I'm doing.
Got invited to speak at the conference and my first thought was that they must be short of speakers.
My friends say I'm a great cook but I always assume they're being polite. Didn't offer to host this time.
Started a new job last week and I'm sure they're already regretting hiring me. Everyone seems to know so much more.
Deleted the email to the professor three times. Who am I to ask for a research placement.

everyday: Did the weekly shop, put a wash on, and made a stir fry for tea.
Dentist at 10, then back to work. Rained most of the afternoon.
Watched the new series everyone's talking about. It was alright.
Moved my desk to the other side of the room. Looks bigger now.
Picked up a parcel from the post office and walked the long way home.
Had leftovers for lunch. Meeting about the Q3 numbers went on for an hour.
Changed the bedsheets, hoovered, and sorted the recycling.
Got the car serviced. Needs new tyres in the spring apparently.
Booked a table for Saturday at the Italian place on the high street.
Bus was busy. Finished my podcast episode about ancient Rome.
Planted some tulip bulbs in the front garden and fixed the gate latch.
Ordered a new phone case and updated my laptop.
